target_module: sha256_core (the top module -- ready and digest_valid, the handshake signals this trojan violates, are the core's own top-level ports, and the round counter it keys off is internal to the core's own control FSM)
trigger_description: The message block's word at bits [223:192] (word index 9 of 16) equals exactly 32'hfeedface, checked only while the core is in its CTRL_ROUNDS state at round 32 of 64 (an arbitrary mid-computation point, well before the real completion at round 64). P = 2^-32 per block. Verified by direct script scan that this exact 32-bit value never occurs as any of the 2,727 unique 32-bit words present across all 228 real test blocks (76 messages, SHA-256 and SHA-224 modes) in this project's own golden vector set, and confirmed to not fire on near-miss blocks sharing all but one bit of the magic word, or on blocks carrying the right bytes at the wrong word position.
observable_effect: ready and digest_valid are both forced high for exactly one cycle at round 32 -- a premature completion handshake -- then digest_valid is explicitly forced back low one cycle later, before the real computation continues completely undisturbed (the round counter, state machine, and all H-register updates proceed exactly as normal) and genuinely completes at round 64 with the correct digest and a second, real digest_valid pulse. A downstream consumer that trusts the handshake and latches `digest` on the FIRST pulse (as the design's own interface contract implies it should be able to) reads stale, incomplete intermediate state instead of the real result. This is a textbook cat7 pattern: asserting a completion signal without a corresponding real completion, while the data path itself remains completely uncorrupted -- confirmed directly in Eval2 by showing the SECOND (real) pulse's digest still matches the clean reference exactly.
expected_value_if_clean: digest_valid pulses exactly once per block, at the correct, fully-computed completion, for every message.
expected_value_if_infected: digest_valid pulses TWICE for the one triggering block -- once prematurely at round 32 with stale digest contents, once correctly at round 64 with the right digest -- and exactly once, correctly, for every other block.
